title: Private deployments network RBAC tracebook + SIEM export schema
body:
Purpose

This is a working tracebook that ties RBAC v2 mappings to network trust boundaries for private deployments, describes the audit-log schema we push to the SIEM, and provides an evidence-automation runbook and hardening checklist for the network layer (VPC, firewall rules, mTLS). Goal is a single reference for engineers and security reviewers to reason about who can do what, how network flows are authorized, and how we collect/verifiably export evidence to customer SIEMs.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood Private (VPC & on-prem) network topology and supporting control plane APIs.
- Covers RBAC v2 principals -> network roles mapping, flow-level firewall patterns, mTLS enforcement points, and SIEM export schema for audit logs and network evidence.
- Does NOT include host-level OS hardening (separate SRE doc) or application-layer auth beyond service-to-service mTLS.

Quick summary of recommendations (TL;DR)
- Authorize by identity first (RBAC v2), then by network policy. Network policies are enforcement, not primary source of truth.
- Emit structured audit events for every policy decision (allow/deny + reason + principal + flow metadata).
- Forward compressed NDJSON to SIEM with sequence numbers and provenance metadata.
- Automate evidence collection via a small agent that produces signed manifests per-checkpoint.

1) RBAC v2 -> Network role mapping (practical guide)

High level: RBAC v2 defines Principals, Roles, and Grants. For private deployments we map Roles to network-level capabilities so a single auth decision can be validated by network enforcers.

Minimal role set (example):
- role:platform-admin -> capability:control-plane-api, debug-bastion-access, audit-read
- role:ops-network -> capability:modify-firewall, read-vpc-metrics, siem-forwarder-manage
- role:svc-inference -> capability:egress-inference-nodes, kv-cache-access
- role:svc-observability -> capability:connect-siem-endpoints, pull-metrics
- role:read-only -> capability:read-only-network-config

Mapping rules:
- Principle-of-least-privilege: map narrow capabilities only. Avoid granting modify-firewall to service accounts unless necessary.
- Bindings must include a "scope" claim (customer_id, vpc_id, region) so network enforcers can evaluate tenancy constraints.
- Every binding must have an "issued_by" and "issued_at" fields and an optional "expiry" for temporary grants.

Example RBAC assertion (stringified claim stored in control plane):
{
  "principal":"svc-inference:redwood-deploy-123",
  "role":"svc-inference",
  "scope":"vpc-az3-456",
  "issued_by":"iam.redwood-internal",
  "issued_at":"2024-11-06T17:05:02Z",
  "expiry":"2025-02-05T17:05:02Z"
}

2) Network enforcement patterns (VPC & firewall rules)

Guiding principle: use identity-aware firewall rules where supported (e.g., service mesh + mTLS + token) and fall back to subnet-level allowlists for legacy customers.

Standard segmented VPC layout (recommended):
- management-subnet (private, 10.10.0.0/24) -> bastion, control-plane endpoints (mTLS enforced)
- infra-subnet (private, 10.10.1.0/24) -> SIEM forwarder, metrics collector
- inference-subnet (private, 10.10.2.0/22) -> inference nodes (GPU), restricted egress rules
- customer-evidence-bucket-subnet (private, 10.10.6.0/26) -> upload checkpoints to customer S3-compatible endpoint (signed)

Firewall rule templates (for a given vpc_id):
- allow inbound: management-subnet -> control-plane-api:443 (mTLS, verify client cert + RBAC assertion header)
- allow outbound: inference-subnet -> kv-cache-service:11211 (internal only, enforce mTLS)
- deny: inference-subnet -> management-subnet (default-deny, exceptions only)
- allow: infra-subnet -> siem-proxy:9200 (TLS, client cert pin)

Notes on rule composition:
- Prefer explicit allow rules + default deny. Document each exception with a Jira ticket id and expiry.
- For cloud providers that support identity tags (e.g., GCP service accounts), mirror RBAC principals into tags and generate rules dynamically.

3) mTLS placement and validation

Where to terminate mTLS:
- Control plane endpoints: mutual TLS validated at the edge (API gateway or Envoy). Validate client cert chain + RBAC assertion header signed by control plane KMS.
- Intra-cluster service-to-service: mTLS inside service mesh (Envoy sidecars), with SDS issuing short-lived certs tied to RBAC role claims.
- SIEM/Forwarder channel: uni-directional mTLS from infra-subnet forwarder to customer SIEM endpoint; forwarder must rotate certs via KMS/HSM integration.

Key validation checks for any mTLS endpoint:
- cert CN/subject alternative name contains principal identifier (consistent canonical form).
- cert issued by our internal CA or a supported customer CA (configurable).
- revocation/OCSP checks where available.
- certificate-bound RBAC assertion header must match cert principal. Reject on mismatch.

4) Audit log / SIEM export schema (NDJSON recommended)

Export requirements: events must be structured, append-only, and cryptographically verifiable for evidence purposes. We export compressed NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) to the SIEM collector. Every line is a self-contained event.

Required fields for each event (flat schema):
- event_id (uuidv4)
- timestamp_utc (ISO 8601)
- event_type (RBAC_DECISION | NETWORK_FLOW | FIREWALL_CHANGE | EVIDENCE_UPLOAD | SIEM_FORWARDER_STATUS)
- principal (string, canonical id)
- role (string)
- vpc_id (string)
- src_ip (ip)
- src_port (int)
- dst_ip (ip)
- dst_port (int)
- protocol (tcp|udp|http/1.1|grpc)
- action (allow|deny|throttle)
- reason (short string; enum where possible)
- policy_id (string; reference to firewall or policy)
- decision_signature (base64) -> HMAC or signature over important fields using agent key
- evidence_manifest_uri (optional) -> signed manifest where captured evidence is stored
- seq_num (monotonic per-vpc, padded as string)

Example NDJSON line (single-line string):
{"event_id":"6a1f3c3a-8c2a-4f7a-9aee-1f2d7d9bfa2b","timestamp_utc":"2024-12-10T01:22:14Z","event_type":"NETWORK_FLOW","principal":"svc-inference:redwood-deploy-123","role":"svc-inference","vpc_id":"vpc-az3-456","src_ip":"10.10.2.11","src_port":"46822","dst_ip":"10.10.1.9","dst_port":"9200","protocol":"tcp","action":"allow","reason":"policy-match:infra-to-siem","policy_id":"fw-2024-1009-ops","decision_signature":"MEUCIQDO...base64...","evidence_manifest_uri":"s3://evidence-bucket/vpc-az3-456/manifests/manifest-20241210.json","seq_num":"0000001234"}

Compression and transport
- We gzip batches (<= 5MB uncompressed) and POST to the customer's SIEM ingestion endpoint. If the customer provides an on-prem collector, we support a signed S3 upload + webhook notification.
- Use TLS1.3 and client certs mutually verified. Retry with exponential backoff; include last_seq_num sent in the next batch header.

5) Evidence automation runbook (low-friction, verifiable checkpoints)

Agent model: a lightweight evidence agent runs in infra-subnet and can be triggered automatically on policy changes, on-demand via control plane, or as part of periodic attestations. The agent produces three artifacts per checkpoint:
- checkpoint-manifest.json (signed manifest listing evidence files, sha256 digests, timestamps, agent id, seq_num)
- network-capture.pcap.gz (limited capture of the flow in question; rotated and TTL'd)
- metadata.json (human-readable audit summary with links to Jira tickets, configuration snapshots)

Checkpoint manifest fields (flat key-value pairs in manifest top-level):
- manifest_id, created_at, agent_id, vpc_id, related_policy_id, seq_num, files:[list-of-uris] (NOTE: in the body we keep as a single-line CSV string for simplicity), signature

Automation steps:
1) Trigger (policy change OR scheduled attestation OR manual).
2) Agent collects config snapshot (iptables, SGs, route tables), short pcap (10s), and logs.
3) Agent uploads artifacts to evidence-bucket with server-side encryption and writes manifest.
4) Agent emits EVIDENCE_UPLOAD event to local event buffer and attempts immediate SIEM forward (compressed NDJSON).
5) Control plane validates manifest signature and links manifest to the RBAC binding for future audits.

Example manifest line (simplified, single-line):
manifest_id=man-20241210-0001,created_at=2024-12-10T01:25:00Z,agent_id=infra-agent-az3-11,vpc_id=vpc-az3-456,related_policy_id=fw-2024-1009-ops,seq_num=0000001234,files=s3://evidence-bucket/...,signature=MEUCIQ...BASE64

6) SIEM mapping and alerts (practical guidance)

Field mapping: map our NDJSON fields into SIEM fields as-is. Create the following alert rules to start: 
- ALERT A1: repeated DENY from same src_ip > 50 events in 5m -> escalate to SOC + open Jira PD-SEC ticket automatically.
- ALERT A2: RBAC_DECISION where role==platform-admin AND action==allow AND src_ip outside management-subnet -> manual verification required.
- ALERT A3: FIREWALL_CHANGE with no linked Jira ticket -> auto-create dev task and notify network-owners.

Retention: keep raw exports for 90 days in the customer's SIEM (or per-customer policy). For evidence artifacts (pcap/manifests) keep at least 180 days or per-contract.

7) Review checklist (hands-on steps for a security review)

Pre-review:
- Verify each firewall rule has policy_id and linked Jira ticket (list IDs).
- Confirm RBAC bindings include scope and expiry for non-service principals.
- Confirm SIEM endpoint and client cert fingerprint recorded in control-plane config.

On-review:
- Pick 3 sample events from recent NDJSON export and validate decision_signature, seq_num monotonicity, and that the manifest file exists in evidence-bucket.
- Validate one RBAC assertion: ensure principal->role->scope map actually exists in control plane and matches cert SAN.
- Query the SIEM for recent FIREWALL_CHANGE events and confirm each has linked_artifact (jira) and manifest where relevant.

Hardening checklist (short):
- [ ] Default deny for inter-subnet flows; exceptions documented with expiry.
- [ ] All control-plane APIs behind mTLS; reject if RBAC assertion header missing or mismatched.
- [ ] SIEM forwarder in infra-subnet with cert pinning and signed batches.
- [ ] Evidence agent signed manifests enabled and verified by control plane.
- [ ] RBAC bindings audited weekly; temporary grants auto-expire.
- [ ] Firewall rule automation pipeline enforces policy_id tagging and human approval for high-risk rules.

8) Troubleshooting notes

- If events stop arriving at SIEM: check forwarder cert rotation, last_seq_num mismatch in headers, and that the forwarder has network path to customer endpoint (traceroute from infra-subnet).
- If evidence manifest fails signature verification: check agent key rotation timeline and KMS access grants; re-run attestation for suspect seq range.

9) Diagram (ASCII) - quick view for reviewers

[customer-onprem]                 [customer-siem-endpoint]
       |                                   ^
       |                                   | mTLS (client cert pin)
   Internet                             infra-subnet:siem-forwarder
       |                                   |
  edge-gw (mTLS) ---- management-subnet ---- control-plane (verify cert + RBAC header)
                             |
                         service-mesh
                             |
                      inference-subnet (GPU nodes)

Notes: control-plane issues short-lived RBAC assertions; service mesh issues SDS certs bound to assertions; forwarder posts compressed NDJSON to customer-siem-endpoint.

10) Open questions / items for follow-up
- How granular should role->policy mapping be for multi-tenant customers who have nested projects within a VPC? Proposal: include project_id in scope and allow policy evaluation to be hierarchical.
- Should we implement per-event signatures (higher cost) vs per-batch HMAC (lower cost)? Need threat-model decision from security.
- Add integration test to CI that spins up a mock SIEM and validates seq_num monotonicity across restart.

Appendix: helpful Jira/Confluence links and quick commands
- confluence:PD-SEC-1823 (RBAC v2 spec)
- jira:PD-3892 (evidence agent work)
- quick check: curl -H 'X-RBACH-Assertion: <base64>' --cert client.pem https://control-plane.example.com/healthz

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a working tracebook — please add comments inline with example policy_ids from current ticket backlog. The intent is to keep the doc compact and actionable for an audit or customer review.
